name: Saratoga
lede: Saratoga is a warm orange-yellow listed in the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930; the books say nothing about where the name came from.

sections.title: A name without a story
sections.body:
The word Saratoga appears in one of our books only as part of a painting's title, *Crew Race, Saratoga, 2005*, so it tells us about a place and nothing about a color [1]. No book we hold explains the color name.

What the record shows is narrower. The Maerz and Paul dictionary lists Saratoga at plate 11, block J 8, and the library gives 1922 as its first recorded use [2]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which cited the Maerz and Paul names, files this swatch under "moderate orange yellow", only 2.8 CIEDE2000 units away [2]. The word may be a place name, but our sources do not say so, and we do not claim it [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Saratoga is fairly common as a painted color [3]. It appears in 680 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 2.86 per cent, more often than 83 per cent of the named colors [3]. In 71 per cent of the 519 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays an accent [3].

It peaks in the 1300s, at 5.2 per cent of the 251 paintings from that century, 2.6 times the museums' baseline [3]. It is most over-represented in Indian paintings, at 3.0 times the expected rate, and it shares canvases with [[copper]] and [[ochre-yellow]] more than chance would predict [3]. Its most devoted painter is Pietro Perugino, in 5 of his 16 works here [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match shows a look-alike hue and not a pigment [3].
